messages:
Rachel: quick heads-up — I ran the asymmetric lazy-decode trial on llamaX-13B-quant (int4) this morning. baseline 1-pass p=0.95, new flow does cheap-prefix -> full-decode fallback. saw ~1.9x avg token throughput on webchat traces but some QA regressions in long-answer subset. thoughts?
Sam: nice, can you paste the simple command you used?
Rachel: sure — run used:
```bash
./run_decode --model llamaX-13b-int4 --mode asymmetric_lazy --cheap-prefix-len 32 --fallback-threshold 0.6 --batch 8 --seed 42
```
Anya: what metric for QA regressions? blue/ROUGE? or task-specific?
Rachel: used our conversational BLEU proxy + F1 on SQuAD-like holdouts. overall BLEU dropped 1.2 pts on long-answer group (>200 tokens), F1 dropped 0.8 on exact-match like spans. for short answers (<40 tokens) no sig change.
Mike: any change in sampling (temp/topk/top-p)? cheap-prefix uses greedy?
Rachel: cheap-prefix was greedy then stochastic fallback. sampling params preserved for full-decode: temp=0.8, top_p=0.95.
Jordan: curious whether quantization (int4) interacts — cheap-prefix may be more brittle if logits small. did you try int8 baseline?
Rachel: good call. I ran int8 full baseline earlier — throughput 1.1x over int4 baseline but quality slightly better. asymmetric on int8 gave ~1.3x speedup only. suggests quant noise amplifies fallback rate.
Sam: what's the fallback rate?
Rachel: ~18% of tokens triggered fallback for long-answer traces, ~3% for short. fallback mostly concentrated in Q->A sections and code blocks.
Anya: can we instrument per-token entropy and top-1 margin before cheap-prefix decision? might tighten threshold selectively.
Rachel: yes, I already dumped per-step logits for 100 traces. sample row:
```
step: 128, top1: 0.42, top2: 0.11, entropy: 3.8, decision: fallback
```
Mike: propose two experiments: (A) raise cheap-prefix-len to 64 and reduce threshold to 0.5; (B) keep len=32 but require margin>0.25 to stay cheap. run both on 10k webchat samples and our long-answer holdout.
Jordan: also add model-agnostic eval: measure pass@1 on code tasks and exact-match on knowledge probes. need to ensure no silent regressions.
Rachel: will run A/B. ETA: initial runs in ~4 hours on staging cluster (using dedicated batch pool). posting raw logs to /mnt/experiments/asymm_lazy/1763200000.
OpsBot: deploy started on cluster-staging-3 by Rachel at 2026-03-21T09:42:01Z :rocket:
Sam: thanks. one more ask — can you track tokens/fallback by prefix type (system vs user vs code)? last time fallbacks spiked on system instructions.
Rachel: yep will break down by role. collecting now.
Anya: ping me when the 10k job finishes, I’ll run the quality diff harness. I can also add a pragmatic heuristic: if cheap-prefix predicts a punctuation-heavy tail, force fallback less often.
Mike: if we can get fallback <=10% on long answers without >0.5 BLEU drop I think it's a keeper. otherwise maybe hybrid: cheap-prefix only for interactive short-turns.
Rachel: agreed. posting intermediate numbers in thread once runs complete. thanks all. :thumbsup:
